correctness.rationale: Writing a=γ+μ, the interior derivatives of logit(n), log I and S+I are respectively ε₂[1+θ−(2+θ)x], βS−a and μ(1−x−S)−aI. With the stated coefficients the x and S terms cancel and the constant is μ/β−μ/[a(2+θ)], giving H'=I−I_c independently of the x equation. Interior initial conditions keep both logs defined over finite times. Integrating against an invariant probability with compact interior support eliminates the bounded endpoint differences, giving ∫I=I_c, ∫x=(1+θ)/(2+θ), ∫S=1/ℛ₀ and, by the I equation, β∫SI=aI_c. Positivity excludes such measures at and below threshold, including criticality. On the entire prescribed strip, the displayed numerator bounds the oscillation of H and (δ−I_c)T≤ΔH, yielding the bound only for δ>I_c. Above threshold S*=1/ℛ₀, x*=(1+θ)/(2+θ), I*=I_c, and R*=1−S*−I*>0 (indeed S*+I*<1/(2+θ)); βI*/(βI*+μ)=f*, so the chosen costs with n*=f* cancel the payoff. These values and the rational example satisfy all equations. No assertion about arbitrary costs, global eradication or boundary-reaching averages is supported. Replay: RESULT.md lines 37–70.
